pages.content: # RoboWorld 2026 Track 1: WorldNav Welcome to WorldNav, the language-conditioned visual navigation track of the RoboWorld 2026, affiliated with the RoboPAD Workshop at NeurIPS 2026. An agent receives one initial egocentric RGB image and a natural-language instruction. It must predict a complete navigation action sequence without a goal image, an initial numeric pose, or further observations from the environment. World models, vision-language-action models, and policy-only methods are welcome. **Important:** To be eligible for the final award ranking, please register your team at https://forms.gle/P2jH3c2VoGsNNWXG8 and make sure to enter the CodaBench team name you use for your submissions. ## Task Definition Submit variable-length sequences of `[dx, dy, dyaw]` actions. `dx` means forward motion and `dy` means leftward motion in the agent's current local frame; `dyaw` changes heading in radians. The private evaluator uses the recorded initial pose to reconstruct the predicted route. Test participants receive only the initial image and instruction, not the pose, goal, reference trajectory, or reference action sequence. ## Phases Phase 1 is for development and validation. Final rankings and awards are based entirely on Phase 2; phase scores are not combined. Phase 1 remains open for validation submissions during Phase 2. | Phase |   | Evaluation data |   | Ranking | |:--|:--:|:--|:--:|:--| | Phase 1: Validation |   | Released `val_seen` and `val_unseen` inputs |   | Mean of `val_seen` and `val_unseen` Scores (50% each) | | Phase 2: Final Evaluation |   | Held-out test inputs |   | Test Score | [Download Phase 2 Test Dataset](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QWGsRBB8KlS_v9Jf0S51C3SpKltL_ZPL?usp=sharing). ## Awards & Recognition Official challenge awards follow the [RoboWorld 2026 Awards & Recognition](https://roboworld2026.github.io/#awards) guidelines: - **Certificates of Recognition**: The **Top 5 teams in each track** will receive official certificates recognizing their achievements in the RoboWorld Challenge 2026. pages.title: Submission & Evaluation
pages.content:
# Submission & Evaluation Submit predicted action sequences in a ZIP archive, using only each episode's initial RGB image and instruction. Each phase allows **5 submissions per day and 200 in total per participant**. ## Action format Each action is [dx, dy, dyaw]: forward displacement, leftward displacement in the agent's **current local frame**, and yaw update in radians. Sequences may have different lengths; the JSON list ends the trajectory. Limits: at most 64 actions per episode; hypot(dx,dy) ≤ 2.46 dataset coordinate units and |dyaw| ≤ 6.29 rad per action (evaluated modulo 2π in [−π, π)). ## ZIP layout ### Phase 2: Final Evaluation Put `test.json` directly at the archive root and include all 15,303 test episodes: ```text submission.zip └── test.json ``` ```bash zip -j submission.zip test.json ``` Download the Phase 2 example ZIP from **Files** and replace its illustrative actions.
Phase 1: Validation archive layout (click to expand) Both `val_seen.json` and `val_unseen.json` are required at the archive root: ```text submission.zip ├── val_seen.json └── val_unseen.json ``` ```bash zip -j submission.zip val_seen.json val_unseen.json ```
### JSON schema Each file contains split and episodes. Include every phase episode_id exactly once, with an actions list: { "split": "test", "episodes": [ { "episode_id": "LCVN_test_00001", "actions": [[0.25, 0.0, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0, 0.15], [0.12, -0.05, 0.0]] } ] } This abbreviated example is not a complete submission. Phase 1 uses the corresponding validation split name and its original episode IDs. ## Evaluation metrics The two fidelity metrics range from 0 to 1. See [demonstration.py](https://github.com/roboworld2026/track1/blob/main/demonstration.py) for the five calculations. | Metric |   | Direction |   | Meaning | | :-- | :--: | :-- | :--: | :-- | | **Success Rate (SR)** |   | Higher |   | Fraction meeting the final-position success criterion. | | **Absolute Trajectory Error (ATE)** |   | Lower |   | Position error over the reference trajectory. | | **Relative Pose Error (RPE)** |   | Lower |   | Relative translation error between consecutive poses. | | **Full-route fidelity** |   | Higher |   | Agreement with the complete ordered recorded route, including a penalty for unnecessary travel. | | **Heading and turn fidelity** |   | Higher |   | Agreement of facing direction while moving and of the direction, position, and amount of turns. | ## Composite Score Each episode is scored first, then the contributions are averaged: Score = (100/N) × Σ_i { FullRouteFidelity_i × (1 + HeadingTurnFidelity_i)/2 × [0.70 + 0.10 SR_i + 0.10/(1+ATE_i) + 0.10/(1+RPE_i)] } SR_i is binary success; ATE_i and RPE_i are per-episode errors in dataset coordinate units. Score averages episode contributions. Phase 1 ranks by `(Score_val_seen + Score_val_unseen) / 2`, with equal weight for each split. Both split files are required; a submission missing either file is rejected. Both split Scores are displayed. Phase 2 ranks by test Score.
pages.content_zh:
# 提交与评估

将预测的动作序列提交至ZIP压缩包，仅使用每个片段的初始RGB图像和指令。

## 动作格式

每个动作为[dx, dy, dyaw]：前向位移、智能体**当前局部坐标系**中的左向位移，以及偏航角更新（弧度制）。序列长度可不同；JSON列表标记轨迹结束。

限制：每个片段最多64个动作；单次动作的hypot(dx,dy) ≤ 2.46数据集坐标单位且|dyaw| ≤ 6.29弧度（在[−π, π)范围内对2π取模计算）。

## ZIP文件结构

将所需的JSON文件置于压缩包根目录。可下载的示例ZIP展示了文件结构和第一阶段片段ID；替换其中的示例动作。

| 阶段 |   | 所需文件 |
| :-- | :--: | :-- |
| 第一阶段 |   | val_seen.json, val_unseen.json |
| 第二阶段 |   | test.json |

### JSON模式

每个文件包含数据集划分和片段。每个阶段的episode_id必须且只能出现一次，附带动作列表：

    {
      "split": "val_unseen",
      "episodes": [
        {
          "episode_id": "20210826_40_0001_02_0",
          "actions": [[0.25, 0.0, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0, 0.15], [0.12, -0.05, 0.0]]
        }
      ]
    }

此简化示例并非完整提交。

## 评估指标

两个保真度指标范围为0到1。五种计算方法参见[demonstration.py](https://github.com/F1y1113/worldnav-challenge/blob/main/demonstration.py)。

| 指标 |   | 方向 |   | 含义 |
| :-- | :--: | :-- | :--: | :-- |
| **成功率 (SR)** |   | 越高越好 |   | 满足最终位置成功标准的比例。 |
| **绝对轨迹误差 (ATE)** |   | 越低越好 |   | 相对于参考轨迹的位置误差。 |
| **相对位姿误差 (RPE)** |   | 越低越好 |   | 连续位姿之间的相对平移误差。 |
| **全路径保真度** |   | 越高越好 |   | 与完整有序记录路径的一致性，包括对不必要移动的惩罚。 |
| **航向与转向保真度** |   | 越高越好 |   | 移动时朝向以及转向方向、位置和幅度的一致性。 |

## 综合得分

首先对每个片段进行评分，然后取平均值：

    Score = (100/N) × Σ_i { FullRouteFidelity_i × (1 + HeadingTurnFidelity_i)/2
                          × [0.70 + 0.10 SR_i + 0.10/(1+ATE_i) + 0.10/(1+RPE_i)] }

SR_i为二元成功标志；ATE_i和RPE_i为每个片段在数据集坐标单位下的误差。得分取各片段贡献的平均值。

第一阶段按`(Score_val_seen + Score_val_unseen) / 2`排名，两个划分权重相等。两个划分的文件都必须提交；缺少任一文件的提交将被拒绝。两个划分的得分均会显示。第二阶段按测试集得分排名。

pages.title: Overview
pages.content: # Welcome to Track 2: HA-VLN **Human-Aware Vision-and-Language Navigation (HA-VLN)** is Track 2 of [RoboWorld 2026](https://roboworld2026.github.io/), affiliated with the [RoboPAD Workshop at NeurIPS 2026](https://robotpad2026.github.io/). **Important:** To be eligible for the final award ranking, please register your team at https://forms.gle/P2jH3c2VoGsNNWXG8 and make sure to enter the CodaBench team name you use for your submissions. ## Challenge Overview This track challenges participants to develop **human-aware vision-and-language navigation agents** that follow natural-language instructions **safely, efficiently, and socially** in dynamic human environments. While many standard VLN benchmarks assume static scenes, real-world spaces are shared with moving people who serve as both semantic landmarks and dynamic obstacles. Built on [HA-VLN 2.0](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14229), submissions must balance **instruction following** and **social compliance** under partial observability and real-time human interactions. - **Human-Referenced Grounding**: Interpret fine-grained instructions that reference both scene landmarks and ongoing human activities. - **Social Norm Compliance**: Respect personal space, proactively avoid human collisions, and navigate safely around moving bystanders. - **Realistic Benchmarking**: Navigate indoor and outdoor areas with multi-human interactions in the HA-R2R and HAPS 2.0 datasets. We welcome navigation policies, waypoint and topological planners, world models, and VLA approaches that advance safe, human-centered navigation in shared spaces. ## Task Definition - **Input:** A natural-language navigation instruction, initial pose and ongoing agent pose (position and heading from simulator state, GPS+compass), and sequential egocentric forward-facing RGB-D observations. Direct access to ground-truth human trajectories (`human_motion.json`) is strictly prohibited during inference. - **Sensor Setup:** One forward-facing RGB-D camera. Adding additional cameras is not permitted; panoramic views must be acquired by rotating in place (rotation actions count toward the action budget). - **Setting:** **Closed-loop interactive navigation** in continuous 3D environments with dynamic humans. - **Actions:** Six discrete actions: `STOP`, `MOVE_FORWARD`, `TURN_LEFT`, `TURN_RIGHT`, `LOOK_UP`, `LOOK_DOWN`. - **Output:** An ordered sequence of 1 to 500 discrete actions for each episode submitted for official simulator replay. Sequences shorter than 500 actions must end in `STOP`; sequences reaching the 500-action limit may omit `STOP`. - **Objective:** Reach the instructed goal safely while avoiding collisions with humans. ## Phases - **Phase 1 (Validation)**: Development on released `val_seen` (778 episodes) and `val_unseen` (1,839 episodes). Both splits are reported; only the `val_unseen` Score determines the Phase 1 ranking. Phase 1 is open until November 23, 2026 (Monday) solely for development and testing, and does not count towards final challenge rankings or awards. - **Phase 2 (Final Evaluation)**: Evaluation on withheld test scoring data (3,408 test episodes). The test Score determines final rankings and awards. All teams are eligible to participate in Phase 2 regardless of Phase 1 participation. [Download Phase 2 Test Dataset](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1HcSg3qCxriEjsgDLlPWBEz9TbgD5RA7W?usp=drive_link). Phase 1 scores do not determine shortlisting or awards and are not combined with Phase 2 scores. Submit at most five times per day and 100 times per phase; the best Score is retained. ## Schedule 1. Registration opens October 08, 2026. 2. Phase 1 opens October 15, 2026, and closes November 23, 2026 (Monday) *(Extended from October 30)*. 3. Phase 2 opens October 30, 2026, and closes November 30, 2026. 4. Award decisions are announced on December 12, 2026. ## Awards & Recognition 1. **Certificates of Recognition**: Official certificates awarded to the Top 5 teams in Track 2. 2. **Best Innovative Solution**: Certificate recognizing outstanding creativity and technical innovation. 3. **Oral Presentations**: Selected top-performing teams will be invited to give oral presentations at the RoboPAD Workshop at NeurIPS 2026. Final rankings and awards are determined entirely by Phase 2 final evaluation. ## Materials & Toolkit - [Challenge repository and participant toolkit](https://github.com/roboworld2026/track2): Documentation, data download scripts, baseline setup, and action submission exporter. - [Phase 2 Official Test Dataset (Google Drive)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1HcSg3qCxriEjsgDLlPWBEz9TbgD5RA7W?usp=drive_link): Official test instructions and human annotations for Phase 2 evaluation. - [Track website](https://roboworld2026.github.io/track2): Official track details and announcements. - [HA-VLN 2.0](https://uwmilab.github.io/HA-VLN-webpage/): Project page and [official repository](https://github.com/UWMILab/HA-VLN). - Starting kits: Download the Phase 2 starting kit attached to this competition for the official test episode manifest, example submission, and local validator (the Phase 1 starting kit remains available for validation development). ## Registration Register your team through the [Google Form](https://roboworld2026.github.io/#registration) (registration opens October 08, 2026) to be eligible for the leaderboard, certificates, and awards. ## Contact - **Frequently Asked Questions:** [Track 2 FAQ](https://github.com/roboworld2026/track2#-frequently-asked-questions) (please check the FAQ before emailing for common questions) - **Technical Support:** [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/roboworld2026/track2/issues) - **Contact Email:** [roboworld2026@gmail.com](mailto:roboworld2026@gmail.com) - **Discord:** [Join the RoboWorld Track 2 Discord](https://discord.gg/S8s8JcxtT) - **WeChat Group:** [Join the RoboWorld Track 2 WeChat Group](https://github.com/roboworld2026/roboworld2026.github.io/blob/main/wechat_track2.JPG)
pages.content_zh:
欢迎来到赛道2：HA-VLN

**具人感知视觉语言导航（HA-VLN）**是 [RoboWorld 2026](https://roboworld2026.github.io/) 的赛道2，隶属于 [NeurIPS 2026 RoboPAD研讨会](https://robotpad2026.github.io/)。

## 挑战赛概述

本赛道要求参赛者开发**具人感知视觉语言导航智能体**，使其能够在动态人体环境中**安全、高效且符合社交规范**地遵循自然语言指令。

尽管许多标准VLN基准测试假设场景是静态的，但真实世界空间与移动的人群共享，这些人既是语义地标也是动态障碍物。基于 [HA-VLN 2.0](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14229)，提交作品必须在部分可观测性和实时人体交互的条件下，平衡**指令遵循**与**社交合规性**。

- **人参考接地**：解读同时参考场景地标和正在进行的人体活动的细粒度指令。
- **社会规范遵守**：尊重个人空间，主动避免与人体碰撞，并安全地绕行移动旁观者。
- **真实基准测试**：在HA-R2R和HAPS 2.0数据集中，在具有多人体交互的室内和室外区域进行导航。

我们欢迎导航策略、路点和拓扑规划器、世界模型以及VLA（视觉语言动作）方法，以推动共享空间中安全、以人为中心的导航技术发展。

## 任务定义

- **输入**：自然语言指令和连续的以自我为中心的RGB-D观测。
- **设置**：在具有动态人体的连续3D环境中进行**闭环交互式导航**。
- **动作**：六个离散动作：`停止`、`前进`、`左转`、`右转`、`抬头`、`低头`。
- **输出**：动作的有序序列（1到500步，以`停止`结束），提交至官方模拟器回放。
- **目标**：安全到达指令目标，同时避免与人体碰撞。

## 阶段

- 第一阶段：在已发布的验证集已见（val_seen）和验证集未见（val_unseen）片段上进行开发。两个划分都会被报告；仅验证集未见的分数决定第一阶段排名。
- 第一阶段覆盖范围：为全部778个验证集已见片段和全部1,839个验证集未见片段提交动作。
- 第二阶段：在保留的测试评分数据上进行最终评估。测试分数决定最终排名和奖项。

第一阶段分数不决定入围或奖项，也不与第二阶段分数合并。每天最多提交5次，每阶段最多提交100次；保留最佳分数。

## 日程安排

1. 报名开始：2026年10月08日。
2. 第一阶段开放：2026年10月15日，截止：2026年10月30日。
3. 第二阶段开放：2026年10月30日，截止：2026年11月30日。
4. 奖项决定公布：2026年12月12日。

## 奖项与认可

1. **认可证书**：颁发给赛道2前5名团队的官方证书。
2. **最佳创新解决方案**：表彰杰出创意和技术创新的证书。
3. **口头报告**：精选的顶尖表现团队将被邀请在NeurIPS 2026 RoboPAD研讨会上进行口头报告。

最终排名和奖项完全由第二阶段测试评估决定。

## 资料与工具包

- [挑战赛代码库和参赛工具包](https://github.com/roboworld2026/track2)：文档、数据下载脚本、基线设置和动作提交导出器。
- [赛道网站](https://roboworld2026.github.io/track2)：官方赛道详情和公告。
- [HA-VLN 2.0](https://uwmilab.github.io/HA-VLN-webpage/)：项目页面和[官方代码库](https://github.com/UWMILab/HA-VLN)。
- 入门套件：下载附加于本次竞赛的第一阶段入门套件，获取官方片段清单、示例提交和本地验证器。

## 报名

通过 [Google表单](https://roboworld2026.github.io/#registration)
（报名开放时间为2026年10月08日）注册您的团队，以获得排行榜、证书和参赛资格。

# Submission & Evaluation Both phases accept a single ZIP archive containing predicted action sequences for all required episodes. ## What the Submission Contains Submit one ZIP archive containing the action sequences for every episode in the phase manifest. > [!NOTE] > - **Phase 1 (Validation)** is open until **November 23, 2026 (Monday)** solely for development and validation testing, and does not determine final challenge awards. > - **Phase 2 (Final Evaluation)** alone determines final rankings and awards. All teams are eligible to participate in Phase 2 regardless of Phase 1 participation. ## Archive Layout ### Phase 2 (Final Evaluation) Place the prediction JSON file directly at the root of the ZIP archive: ```text submission.zip `-- test.json # 3,408 test episodes ``` Package Phase 2 predictions: ```bash zip -j submission.zip test.json ```
Phase 1 (Validation) Archive Layout (Click to expand) For Phase 1 validation development, place both validation split predictions at the archive root: ```text submission.zip |-- val_seen.json # 778 episodes `-- val_unseen.json # 1,839 episodes ``` Package Phase 1 predictions: ```bash zip -j submission.zip val_seen.json val_unseen.json ```
## Prediction File Structure Each JSON file must contain `format_version`, `split`, and `episodes`: ```json { "format_version": 1, "split": "test", "episodes": [ { "episode_id": "1", "actions": ["MOVE_FORWARD", "TURN_LEFT", "LOOK_UP", "LOOK_DOWN", "STOP"] } ] } ``` - `format_version`: Set to `1`. - `split`: Set to `"test"` for Phase 2 (3,408 episodes). For Phase 1 validation, use `"val_seen"` (778 episodes) and `"val_unseen"` (1,839 episodes). - `episodes`: A list of episode predictions covering all required episode IDs in the phase manifest. - `episode_id`: String identifier matching the manifest exactly once. - `actions`: An ordered list of 1 to 500 actions chosen from `["STOP", "MOVE_FORWARD", "TURN_LEFT", "TURN_RIGHT", "LOOK_UP", "LOOK_DOWN"]`. `"STOP"` may only appear as the final action. Sequences shorter than 500 actions must end with `"STOP"`; sequences reaching the 500-action limit may omit `"STOP"` if terminated by the step limit. ## Pre-upload Verification Before submitting to CodaBench, verify your archive using `check_submission.py` provided in the Starting Kit: ```bash python3 check_submission.py submission.zip ``` The checker validates archive integrity, JSON schema, action vocabulary, STOP placement, and episode coverage without requiring a GPU or simulator. ## Evaluation & Leaderboard Submissions are evaluated on navigation and social compliance, and ranked by the composite challenge **Score** (higher is better): - **SR** (higher is better): Collision-free navigation success rate to the target goal. - **NE** (lower is better): Mean Euclidean distance in metres from final agent position to goal. - **CR** (lower is better): Ratio of collision episodes over human-influenced episodes. - **TCR** (lower is better): Mean number of collision events per episode. ```text NE utility = 3 / (3 + NE) TCR utility = 1 / (1 + TCR) Navigation = 0.80 * SR + 0.20 * NE utility Social = 0.75 * (1 - CR) + 0.25 * TCR utility Score = 100 * Navigation * (0.70 + 0.30 * Social) ``` Phase 1 ranks teams by `val_unseen` Score (`val_seen` is reported for reference). Phase 2 ranks teams by `test` Score to determine final awards. When Scores are tied, rankings are broken in order: higher SR, lower NE, lower CR, lower TCR, and earlier submission time. Official evaluation replays submitted action sequences in the organizer-controlled CodaBench environment under standardized conditions. Human animations advance with wall-clock time according to the configured motion FPS (rather than advancing one frame per action). Official CodaBench replay results determine official competition rankings. ## Submission Limits Each team may submit up to 5 times per day and 100 times per phase. The leaderboard retains the team's highest Score. ## Support - **Frequently Asked Questions:** [Track 2 FAQ](https://github.com/roboworld2026/track2#-frequently-asked-questions) (please check the FAQ before emailing for common questions) - **Technical Support:** [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/roboworld2026/track2/issues) - **Contact Email:** [roboworld2026@gmail.com](mailto:roboworld2026@gmail.com)

# 提交与评估

两个阶段均接受包含所有所需回合预测动作序列的单个ZIP压缩包。

## 提交内容

提交一个ZIP压缩包，包含阶段清单中每个回合的动作序列。评估仅使用动作预测结果；无需提供模型权重、代码和外部环境资源。

## 归档结构

将预测JSON文件直接放在ZIP压缩包的根目录下：

```text
submission.zip
|-- val_seen.json      # 778 episodes
`-- val_unseen.json    # 1,839 episodes
```

第二阶段遵循相同的结构，在`submission_test.zip`中包含`test.json`。打包第一阶段预测结果：

```bash
zip -j submission.zip val_seen.json val_unseen.json
```

## 预测文件结构

每个JSON文件必须包含`format_version`、`split`和`episodes`：

```json
{
  "format_version": 1,
  "split": "val_unseen",
  "episodes": [
    {
      "episode_id": "synthetic-example-001",
      "actions": ["MOVE_FORWARD", "TURN_LEFT", "LOOK_UP", "LOOK_DOWN", "STOP"]
    }
  ]
}
```

- `format_version`：设置为`1`。
- `split`：`"val_seen"`、`"val_unseen"`或`"test"`，与对应阶段匹配。
- `episodes`：包含清单中所有回合ID的预测列表。
  - `episode_id`：与清单完全匹配的字符串标识符，每个回合只出现一次。
  - `actions`：从`["STOP", "MOVE_FORWARD", "TURN_LEFT", "TURN_RIGHT", "LOOK_UP", "LOOK_DOWN"]`中选择的1至500个动作的有序列表。`"STOP"`只能作为最后一个动作出现；短于500个动作的序列必须以`"STOP"`结尾。

## 评估与排行榜

提交结果根据导航和社交合规性进行评估，并按综合挑战**分数**进行排名（越高越好）：

- **SR**（越高越好）：到达目标的无碰撞导航成功率。
- **NE**（越低越好）：智能体最终位置到目标的平均欧几里得距离（米）。
- **CR**（越低越好）：碰撞回合与受人类影响回合的比率。
- **TCR**（越低越好）：每回合的平均碰撞事件次数。

```text
NE utility  = 3 / (3 + NE)
TCR utility = 1 / (1 + TCR)
Navigation  = 0.80 * SR + 0.20 * NE utility
Social      = 0.75 * (1 - CR) + 0.25 * TCR utility
Score       = 100 * Navigation * (0.70 + 0.30 * Social)
```

第一阶段根据`val_unseen`分数对队伍进行排名（`val_seen`分数仅供参考）。第二阶段根据`test`分数对队伍进行排名以确定最终奖项。当分数相同时，按以下顺序打破平局：更高的SR、更低的NE、更低的CR、更低的TCR、更早的提交时间。

## 提交限制

每支队伍每天最多可提交5次，每个阶段最多可提交100次。排行榜保留队伍的最高分数。

## 技术支持

- **技术支持：** [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/roboworld2026/track2/issues)  
- **赛事与注册：** [roboworld2026@gmail.com](mailto:roboworld2026@gmail.com)

pages.content:
# 🩺 
# **OncoSegment: Breast Tumor Mapping Challenge**

# 💡 
## **Why this Problem is Interesting**

Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of death among women worldwide. Early and accurate detection through ultrasound is critical, but interpreting these images is notoriously difficult.Ultrasound images suffer from "speckle noise" and low contrast. Much like the "blobs" in plasma physics simulations, tumors in ultrasound are intermittent, have irregular boundaries, and can be easily confused with healthy tissue. This challenge asks you to develop an AI that can precisely outline tumor boundaries, a task that directly assists radiologists in biopsy planning and treatment.

# 📊 
## **The Data**

The dataset is derived from the Breast Ultrasound Images (BUSI) collection, featuring women aged 25–75. It consists of high-quality PNG scans with a standard resolution (approx. 500x500 px).

Dataset Breakdown:

Benign: Tumors that are typically oval or round with smooth edges.

Malignant: Cancerous tumors, often characterized by "spiky" (spiculated) or irregular borders that invade surrounding tissue.

Normal: Scans with no tumors (used to test your model's ability to avoid False Positives).

What you receive in the Starting Kit:
train_images: A list of PIL images (Grayscale) showing the breast 
tissue.
train_masks: Binary masks where 1 represents the tumor and 0 represents the background.
train_labels: Metadata identifying the tumor as benign or malignant.
test_images: Images where you must predict the mask.

 # 📏 
## **Metrics: Measuring Precision**

In medical imaging, a "box" is not enough. We need to know exactly which pixels are cancerous. We use two complementary overlap metrics:
1. Primary Metric: Dice Coefficient (F1-Score)The Dice coefficient is the gold standard for medical segmentation. It is twice the area of overlap divided by the total number of pixels in both the prediction and the ground truth.
$$Dice = \frac{2 \times |P \cap G|}{|P| + |G|}$$
Why? It is highly sensitive to the internal "fullness" of the mask and rewards models that get the shape exactly right.
2. Secondary Metric: Jaccard Index (IoU)
The Jaccard index is the area of intersection divided by the area of union.
$$Jaccard = \frac{|P \cap G|}{|P \cup G|}$$
Why? 
It is more "punishing" than Dice for small errors.
It helps break ties on the leaderboard by highlighting models with the fewest stray False Positive pixels.

# 🩺 
# **OncoSegment：乳腺肿瘤分割挑战赛**

# 💡 
## **为什么这个问题很有意义**

乳腺癌仍然是全球女性死亡的主要原因之一。通过超声进行早期准确检测至关重要，但解读这些图像出了名的困难。超声图像存在"散斑噪声"和对比度低的问题。就像等离子体物理模拟中的"团块"一样，超声中的肿瘤呈散在分布，边界不规则，很容易与健康组织混淆。本挑战赛要求你开发一种能够精确勾画肿瘤边界的AI，这项任务直接协助放射科医生进行活检规划和治疗。

# 📊 
## **数据**

该数据集源自乳腺超声图像（BUSI）数据集，涵盖25-75岁女性。它由高质量的PNG扫描图像组成，标准分辨率约为500×500像素。

数据集分类：

良性：通常为椭圆形或圆形、边缘光滑的肿瘤。

恶性：癌性肿瘤，通常以"棘状"（毛刺状）或不规则边界为特征，侵袭周围组织。

正常：没有肿瘤的扫描图像（用于测试模型避免假阳性的能力）。

入门套件提供的内容：
train_images：一组显示乳腺组织的PIL图像（灰度）。
train_masks：二值掩膜，其中1代表肿瘤，0代表背景。
train_labels：识别肿瘤为良性或恶性的元数据。
test_images：你需要预测其掩膜的图像。

 # 📏 
## **评估指标：衡量精确度**

在医学影像中，仅用一个"框"是不够的。我们需要准确知道哪些像素是癌变的。我们使用两种互补的重叠指标：
1. 主要指标：Dice系数（F1分数）Dice系数是医学分割的金标准。它是预测掩膜与真实掩膜重叠区域面积的两倍，除以两者像素总数。
$$Dice = \frac{2 \times |P \cap G|}{|P| + |G|}$$
为什么？它对掩膜内部的"饱满度"非常敏感，并奖励那些能准确把握形状的模型。
2. 次要指标：Jaccard指数（IoU）
Jaccard指数是交集面积除以并集面积。
$$Jaccard = \frac{|P \cap G|}{|P \cup G|}$$
为什么？
对于微小的错误，它比Dice更"惩罚性强"。
它通过突出显示具有最少游离假阳性像素的模型，帮助在排行榜上打破平局。

pages.content:
# Food Image Benchmark: Developing Digital Biomarkers (363-1163-00L)

From **one photo of a meal**, can a model tell what is on the plate, how much of
each food there is, and what that means for health?

This is the common benchmark of the group biomarker project. Every group takes
part in **Task 1**. Each group also takes part in **one Task 2 target**.

| | What you predict per meal | Leaderboard metrics |
|---|---|---|
| **Task 1: ingredients and portions** | a dict of free-text ingredient names and grams | food-group F1, ingredient F1, total-weight wMAPE |
| **Task 2: carbohydrate** | carbohydrate (g) | MAE |
| **Task 2: protein** | protein (g) | MAE |
| **Task 2: diet quality** | HEI-FG diet-quality score (0–100) | HEI-FG |

All results share one leaderboard table. Look at the columns for your task.

## Timeline

| Date | |
|---|---|
| 04.11 | Benchmark opens |
| 25.11 | Class data released (scored by you with the course scoring code) |
| 16.12 | Benchmark closes; report and presentations |

## How it works

1. Download the data on the **Files** tab: 2,923 training meals with labels
   and 974 validation meals without labels.
2. Build your method on the training set.
3. Predict the 974 validation meals: fill in `validation_template.csv` (one row
   per meal), zip it and upload it under **My Submissions**.
4. The platform scores your file against the hidden labels. Your latest scored
   submission appears on the leaderboard, next to the three references.

You can submit up to 5 times a day. Spend model calls wisely: the free tiers are
limited.

## References on the leaderboard

| | T1 · group F1 | T1 · ingredient F1 | T1 · weight wMAPE | Carb MAE | Protein MAE | HEI-FG |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| No-skill baseline | 0.27 | 0.19 | 49.8 % | 13.7 g | 14.6 g | 11.5 |
| Zero-shot Gemini 3 Flash | 0.65 | 0.52 | 34.2 % | 9.0 g | 7.4 g | 9.2 |
| NutriLens (Gemini 3 Flash, optimised prompt) | 0.70 | 0.52 | 29.5 % | 7.9 g | 7.3 g | 8.7 |

The **no-skill baseline** uses only the training data. For each source it
predicts the most common components and the average values.
**Zero-shot Gemini 3 Flash** is a single prompt with no examples. It returns
ingredient names, a total weight and nutrient totals, but no grams per
ingredient, so its weight was split equally across its ingredients. Its HEI-FG was
computed from its ingredients with `diet_quality.py`.
**NutriLens** is the nutrition-estimation module of the NutriLens study: the same
model with a prompt optimised for this task. It returns each ingredient with its
grams, and its HEI-FG was computed the same way. Its prompt was tuned on 100
meals, 24 of which are in the validation set, so its score here is slightly
optimistic.

pages.title: Data
pages.content:
# Data

**Download:** `food_benchmark.zip` in the **Files** tab, about 300 MB.

3,897 meal photos from two public datasets, cleaned as in the NutriLens study:
**Nutrition5k** (overhead photos of cafeteria plates, with weighed ingredients) and
the **January Food Benchmark** (everyday phone photos, with human-validated
annotations).

| | Nutrition5k | January | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Training set (labels given) | 2,271 | 652 | 2,923 |
| Validation set (labels hidden) | 757 | 217 | 974 |

Each source was split 75/25, stratified by main macronutrient, number of
ingredients and meal-weight quartile, so both sets look alike. Images are JPEGs
with a long side of at most 1024 px and no metadata. Meal IDs are random.

## Files

```
training/images/TR-XXXX.jpg   training photos
training_meals.csv             one row per training meal: totals and targets
training_components.csv        one row per component of each training meal
validation/images/VAL-XXXX.jpg    validation photos
validation_template.csv           the file you fill in and upload: one row per validation meal
sample_submission.csv             a complete, valid example (the no-skill baseline)
food_groups.csv                   the course food-group taxonomy (33 groups)
ground_truth_names.csv            training-set ingredient names and their food groups
diet_quality.py                   computes the HEI-FG score from ingredients and grams
```

### `training_components.csv`

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `meal_id` | meal ID |
| `component` | component name (cleaned) |
| `food_group` | group from `food_groups.csv` |
| `grams` | weight of the component |
| `energy_kcal`, `carb_g`, `protein_g`, `fat_g` | nutrients of this component |
| `original_name` | name in the source dataset |

### `training_meals.csv`

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `meal_id`, `source` | meal ID; `n5k` or `january` |
| `ingredients` | the true ingredients and grams, in the same dict format you submit |
| `total_mass_g` | total weight (sum of component grams) |
| `carb_g`, `protein_g` | Task 2 targets (g) |
| `hei_fg` | Task 2 diet-quality target (0–100; blank for meals under 100 kcal) |
| `hei_total_fruit` … `hei_refined_grain` | the 9 HEI-FG component points that add up to `hei_fg` |
| `energy_kcal`, `fat_g`, `fiber_g`, `n_components` | extra labels, not scored |

## Diet quality: HEI-FG

The **HEI-FG** is the food-group part of the **Healthy Eating Index-2020**, the
USDA/NCI index that measures how well food choices follow the Dietary Guidelines.
The HEI scores food-group **density per 1,000 kcal**. A meal's score depends on
its composition, not its size, so it can be applied to a single meal.

| Component | Max points | Full points at (per 1,000 kcal) |
|---|---:|---|
| Total fruits | 5 | ≥ 0.8 cup-eq |
| Whole fruits | 5 | ≥ 0.4 cup-eq |
| Total vegetables | 5 | ≥ 1.1 cup-eq |
| Greens and beans | 5 | ≥ 0.2 cup-eq |
| Whole grains | 10 | ≥ 1.5 oz-eq |
| Dairy | 10 | ≥ 1.3 cup-eq |
| Total protein foods | 5 | ≥ 2.5 oz-eq |
| Seafood and plant proteins | 5 | ≥ 0.8 oz-eq |
| Refined grains (limit) | 10 | ≤ 1.8 oz-eq (0 points at ≥ 4.3) |

Points are linear between the standards, and HEI-FG = 100 × points / 60. The
four HEI nutrient components (added sugars, sodium, saturated fat, fatty-acid
ratio) are left out, because the labels have no data for them. Meals under
100 kcal get no score and are not scored on the leaderboard.

Grams are converted to cup- and ounce-equivalents with fixed factors based on
the USDA Food Patterns Equivalents Database (for example, fruit 150 g, raw
leafy greens 60 g, cooked rice or pasta 80 g per oz-eq, meat 28 g per oz-eq).
Common composite dishes such as pizza and Caesar salad are split with fixed
recipes. Everything is in `diet_quality.py`, so you can compute HEI-FG from your
own Task 1 output: `hei_fg([(name, food_group, grams), ...], kcal)`. Get the
food groups for your names with the evaluator's mapper (`group_mapper.py`).

## Notes on the ground truth

- Ground truth includes small, invisible items such as salt, pepper, oil and
  herbs, and they all count. Nutrition5k lists them often.
- A few meals in the source data have an unusable ingredient label. That label
  is not scored, but its grams still count toward total weight.

## Credits

Nutrition5k: Thames et al., CVPR 2021 (CC BY 4.0). January Food Benchmark:
Hosseinian et al., arXiv:2508.09966 (2025). HEI-2020: Shams-White et al.,
J Acad Nutr Diet 2023. Label cleaning, January ingredient masses and the split:
the NutriLens study (ETH Zurich / CDHI). Use the data for this course only.

# 数据

**下载：** 在 **Files** 标签页中的 `food_benchmark.zip`，约 300 MB。

3,897 张餐食照片，来自两个公开数据集，按照 NutriLens 研究中的方式进行清洗：**Nutrition5k**（食堂餐盘的俯视照片，含称重配料）和 **January Food Benchmark**（日常手机拍摄照片，含人工验证的标注）。

| | Nutrition5k | January | 总计 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 训练集（提供标签） | 2,271 | 652 | 2,923 |
| 验证集（隐藏标签） | 757 | 217 | 974 |

每个数据源按 75/25 的比例划分，按照主要宏量营养素、配料数量和餐食重量四分位数进行分层，因此两组数据分布相似。图像为 JPEG 格式，长边最大 1024 像素，无元数据。餐食 ID 为随机生成。

## 文件

```
training/images/TR-XXXX.jpg   训练照片
training_meals.csv             每行对应一餐训练数据：总计值和目标值
training_components.csv        每行对应训练餐食的一个组成部分
validation/images/VAL-XXXX.jpg    验证照片
validation_template.csv           你填写并上传的文件：每行对应一餐验证数据
sample_submission.csv             一个完整有效的示例（无技能基线）
food_groups.csv                   食物组分类体系（33 个组）
ground_truth_names.csv            训练集中的配料名称及其所属食物组
diet_quality.py                   根据配料和克数计算 HEI-FG 分数
```

### `training_components.csv`

| 列名 | 含义 |
|---|---|
| `meal_id` | 餐食 ID |
| `component` | 组成部分名称（已清洗） |
| `food_group` | 来自 `food_groups.csv` 的组别 |
| `grams` | 组成部分的重量 |
| `energy_kcal`, `carb_g`, `protein_g`, `fat_g` | 该组成部分的营养素 |
| `original_name` | 源数据集中的名称 |

### `training_meals.csv`

| 列名 | 含义 |
|---|---|
| `meal_id`, `source` | 餐食 ID；`n5k` 或 `january` |
| `ingredients` | 真实的配料和克数，采用与你提交格式相同的字典格式 |
| `total_mass_g` | 总重量（组成部分克数之和） |
| `carb_g`, `protein_g` | 任务 2 的目标值（克） |
| `hei_fg` | 任务 2 的饮食质量目标值（0–100；低于 100 千卡的餐食留空） |
| `hei_total_fruit` … `hei_refined_grain` | 9 个 HEI-FG 组成部分分数，相加等于 `hei_fg` |
| `energy_kcal`, `fat_g`, `fiber_g`, `n_components` | 额外标签，不计分 |

## 饮食质量：HEI-FG

**HEI-FG** 是 **Healthy Eating Index-2020（健康饮食指数-2020）** 的食物组部分，是由 USDA/NCI 制定的指数，用于衡量食物选择在多大程度上遵循膳食指南。HEI 对食物组按**每 1,000 千卡的密度**进行评分。餐食的分数取决于其组成，而非份量大小，因此可应用于单餐。

| 组成部分 | 最高分数 | 满分标准（每 1,000 千卡） |
|---|---:|---|
| 总水果 | 5 | ≥ 0.8 cup-eq（杯当量） |
| 完整水果 | 5 | ≥ 0.4 cup-eq |
| 总蔬菜 | 5 | ≥ 1.1 cup-eq |
| 深色蔬菜和豆类 | 5 | ≥ 0.2 cup-eq |
| 全谷物 | 10 | ≥ 1.5 oz-eq（盎司当量） |
| 乳制品 | 10 | ≥ 1.3 cup-eq |
| 总蛋白质食物 | 5 | ≥ 2.5 oz-eq |
| 海鲜和植物蛋白 | 5 | ≥ 0.8 oz-eq |
| 精制谷物（限制） | 10 | ≤ 1.8 oz-eq（≥ 4.3 时得 0 分） |

分数在标准之间呈线性变化，HEI-FG = 100 × 分数 / 60。四个 HEI 营养素组成部分（添加糖、钠、饱和脂肪、脂肪酸比例）被省略，因为标签中没有这些数据。低于 100 千卡的餐食无分数，且在排行榜上不予计分。

克数依据 USDA 食物模式当量数据库通过固定系数转换为杯和盎司当量（例如，水果 150 克，生叶类蔬菜 60 克，熟米饭或面食 80 克每 oz-eq，肉类 28 克每 oz-eq）。常见的复合菜肴（如披萨和凯撒沙拉）按固定配方拆分。所有逻辑均在 `diet_quality.py` 中，因此你可以根据自己的任务 1 输出计算 HEI-FG：`hei_fg([(name, food_group, grams), ...], kcal)`。使用评估器的映射器（`group_mapper.py`）获取配料名称对应的食物组。

## 关于真实标签的说明

- Ground

pages.content:
# Evaluation and submission format

## One file, one row per meal

Fill in `validation_template.csv`: one row for each of the 974 validation meals.
Zip it and upload the zip (`zip submission.zip predictions.csv`). The file name
doesn't matter, but the zip must contain exactly one CSV.

```
meal_id,source,ingredients,carb_g,protein_g,hei_fg
VAL-0001,january,"{""white rice"": 180, ""grilled chicken breast"": 120, ""steamed broccoli"": 80}",,41.5,
VAL-0002,n5k,"{""margherita pizza"": 150}",,12.0,
```

| Column | Task | What to write |
|---|---|---|
| `ingredients` | Task 1 | a dict of **free-text ingredient names → estimated grams**, as JSON (`{"rice": 150, "chicken": 100}`). Write `{}` for a plate with no ingredients. |
| `carb_g` | Task 2 | carbohydrate (g) |
| `protein_g` | Task 2 | protein (g) |
| `hei_fg` | Task 2 | HEI-FG diet-quality score, 0–100 (see **Data**) |

Fill `ingredients` and **your group's Task 2 column**; leave the other columns
blank. A blank column is "not submitted". A column you fill must have a value
for every meal. Numbers must be ≥ 0. With pandas, writing the dict with
`json.dumps(...)` and saving with `to_csv` produces the right quoting.

## Task 1 scores

You give only names and grams. The evaluator does the rest:

| Column | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Food-group F1** | The evaluator maps each of your ingredient names to a course food group (see below). For each meal it compares the set of true food groups with your set: F1 = 2·TP / (2·TP + FN + FP). Averaged over meals. Higher is better. |
| **Ingredient F1** | The same calculation on the ingredients themselves, with no grouping: each of your names is matched to at most one true ingredient. Higher is better. |
| Missed / Hallucinated | Totals over all meals: true ingredients you didn't list (FN), and listed ingredients that aren't in the meal (FP) |
| Unmapped names | How many of your names the evaluator couldn't place in a food group. They're left out of the food-group F1 (no credit, no penalty) but still count for ingredient F1. |
| **Total weight wMAPE** | 100 × Σ\|M − M̂\| / Σ M, where M is a meal's total weight (the sum of its grams). Lower is better. |
| Weight MAE / bias | mean \|M − M̂\| and mean (M̂ − M), in grams |
| Matched-ingredient wMAPE | the grams error on the ingredients you identified correctly |

### How a name is matched to a true ingredient (ingredient F1)

1. **Normalising.** Names are lower-cased, plurals made singular, and common
   synonyms unified ("aubergine" = "eggplant", "scallion" = "green onion",
   "yam" = "sweet potato"). Preparation and cut words are removed ("grilled",
   "sliced", "breast", "fillet"). Words that change the food are kept ("fried
   rice", "brown rice", "sweet potato").
2. **Matching.** Two names match if they're equal, or if one contains all words
   of the other and they share the main food word ("rice" = "white rice",
   "chicken" = "grilled chicken breast"). A modifier that makes a different food
   blocks the match ("peanut butter" ≠ "butter", "almond milk" ≠ "milk").
3. **Generic names and typos.** A generic name matches the specific foods it
   covers ("berries" = "strawberries", "herbs" = "parsley", "fish" = "salmon").
   Small spelling errors are tolerated ("brocoli").
4. **One-to-one.** Within a meal, each true ingredient can be matched once.

### How a name is mapped to a food group (food-group F1)

1. If the name (after normalising) appears in `ground_truth_names.csv`, its
   group is used.
2. Otherwise the course taxonomy's keyword rules are applied (for example, a
   name containing "chicken" → poultry, "lentil" → legumes_soy).
3. Otherwise the matching rules above are tried against the known names.
4. Otherwise the name is "not mapped".

On held-out names, this mapping agrees with the curated ground truth for 99.98%
of ingredients. The code is `matching.py`, `group_mapper.py` and `taxonomy.py` in
the starting kit.

## Task 2 scores

Each filled column shows the **MAE**, which ranks the groups, and the **bias**
(mean of prediction − truth; positive means you over-estimate). For `hei_fg`,
meals under 100 kcal have no true score and are skipped, so give them any value.

## Columns you didn't submit

They show **0** (F1) or **999** (errors and counts), so they sort to the bottom.
This means "not submitted", not a real score.

## Check before you upload

`score_local.py` in the starting kit runs the same scoring program on
training meals you held out. If an upload fails, the error log on
**My Submissions** says why (for example, a missing meal, a value that isn't a
number, or an `ingredients` cell that isn't a dict).

# 评估与提交格式

## 一个文件，每餐一行

填写 `validation_template.csv`：974份验证餐食每餐一行。
将其压缩并上传压缩包（`zip submission.zip predictions.csv`）。文件名
无关紧要，但压缩包必须恰好包含一个CSV文件。

```
meal_id,source,ingredients,carb_g,protein_g,hei_fg
VAL-0001,january,"{""white rice"": 180, ""grilled chicken breast"": 120, ""steamed broccoli"": 80}",,41.5,
VAL-0002,n5k,"{""margherita pizza"": 150}",,12.0,
```

| 列 | 任务 | 填写内容 |
|---|---|---|
| `ingredients` | 任务1 | 一个字典，内容为**自由文本食材名称 → 估计克数**，JSON格式（`{"rice": 150, "chicken": 100}`）。空盘填写 `{}`。 |
| `carb_g` | 任务2 | 碳水化合物（克） |
| `protein_g` | 任务2 | 蛋白质（克） |
| `hei_fg` | 任务2 | HEI-FG饮食质量评分，0–100（见**数据**） |

填写 `ingredients` 和**您小组的任务2对应列**；其他列留空。
留空表示"未提交"。填写的列必须为每餐都提供数值。数字必须 ≥ 0。
使用pandas时，用 `json.dumps(...)` 写入字典并用 `to_csv` 保存可生成正确的引号。

## 任务1评分

您只需提供名称和克数。评估器完成其余工作：

| 列 | 定义 |
|---|---|
| **食物组F1** | 评估器将您的每个食材名称映射到课程食物组（见下文）。对每餐比较真实食物组集合与您的集合：F1 = 2·TP / (2·TP + FN + FP)。取每餐平均值。越高越好。 |
| **食材F1** | 对食材本身进行相同计算，不分组：您的每个名称最多匹配一个真实食材。越高越好。 |
| 遗漏/虚构 | 所有餐食总计：您未列出的真实食材（FN），以及您列出但餐食中不存在的食材（FP） |
| 未映射名称 | 评估器无法归入食物组的您的名称数量。这些不计入食物组F1（无加分，无惩罚），但仍计入食材F1。 |
| **总重量wMAPE** | 100 × Σ\|M − M̂\| / Σ M，其中M为餐食总重量（克数之和）。越低越好。 |
| 重量MAE/偏差 | 平均 \|M − M̂\| 和平均 (M̂ − M)，单位为克 |
| 已匹配食材wMAPE | 您正确识别的食材的克数误差 |

### 名称如何匹配到真实食材（食材F1）

1. **规范化。** 名称转为小写，复数变单数，统一常见同义词（"aubergine" = "eggplant"，"scallion" = "green onion"，"yam" = "sweet potato"）。去除制备和切割词汇（"grilled"、"sliced"、"breast"、"fillet"）。保留改变食物的词汇（"fried rice"、"brown rice"、"sweet potato"）。
2. **匹配。** 两个名称相等则匹配，或若一方包含另一方的所有词汇且共享主要食物词汇则匹配（"rice" = "white rice"，"chicken" = "grilled chicken breast"）。产生不同食物的修饰词会阻止匹配（"peanut butter" ≠ "butter"，"almond milk" ≠ "milk"）。
3. **通用名称和拼写错误。** 通用名称匹配其涵盖的具体食物（"berries" = "strawberries"，"herbs" = "parsley"，"fish" = "salmon"）。允许轻微拼写错误（"brocoli"）。
4. **一对一。** 每餐内，每个真实食材只能匹配一次。

### 名称如何映射到食物组（食物组F1）

1. 若名称（规范化后）出现在 `ground_truth_names.csv` 中，使用其所属组。
2. 否则应用课程分类法的关键词规则（例如，含"chicken"的名称 → 禽肉，"lentil" → 豆类_大豆）。
3. 否则尝试用上述匹配规则对照已知名称。
4. 否则该名称为"未映射"。

在保留名称上，此映射与人工整理的真实值一致率达99.98%。
代码位于起始工具包的 `matching.py`、`group_mapper.py` 和 `taxonomy.py` 中。

## 任务2评分

每个填写列显示**MAE**（平均绝对误差），用于排名。

pages.title: Rules
pages.content:
# Rules

1. **No validation labels.** Both source datasets are public. Don't look up,
   match or retrieve the validation photos or their labels from the original
   releases or anywhere else.
2. **Models.** Gemini through the Google AI Studio free tier, open-weight
   vision-language models (e.g. Gemma 3, Qwen-VL) and any method you train on
   the training set are allowed. Your report must name the model, its version
   and the dates of the calls.
3. **One account per group.** Submit under your group's account only.
4. **Reproducibility.** Your GitHub repository must reproduce your leaderboard
   result: scripts plus cached model outputs.
5. **Data use.** Use the data only for this course, and cite Nutrition5k and the
   January Food Benchmark.

2. **模型。** 允许使用 Google AI Studio 免费版的 Gemini、开源权重视觉-语言模型（例如 Gemma 3、Qwen-VL）以及在训练集上训练的任何方法。报告必须注明模型名称、版本及调用日期。

pages.content:
# How to Participate

## Step 1: Create a Codabench Account

Visit Codabench.org and click Sign Up in the upper right corner. You will need to provide a name and a valid email address. Once registered, you can browse and join any public benchmark.

## Step 2: Register for Ego-IRGBench

Go to the Ego-IRG Challenge competition page and click the My Submissions tab. You will be prompted to accept the competition's Terms and Conditions. Since this is a public challenge with auto-approval enabled, you will be able to participate immediately after accepting the rules.

## Step 3: Download the Dataset and Prepare Your Model

The Ego-IRGBench dataset is hosted on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/yuki3585/Ego-IEGBench). Download and prepare the data according to the instructions in the official [ANNEXE repository](https://yuggiehk.github.io/annexe/). The dataset contains over 20k egocentric images with 1.6M query-answer-mask pairs, organized into train, validation, and test splits.

Train your model on the training set and generate predictions on the test set.

## Step 4: Prepare Your Submission ZIP

Your submission must be a single ZIP file (.zip) with the following structure:

```text
submission/
├── results.json            # Main results file (required)
├── mask/                   # Predicted pixel grounding masks (required)
│   ├── <query_id>.png
│   └── ...
├── depth/                  # Predicted depth maps (optional)
│   └── <image_id>.png
└── README.md               # Method summary (optional)
```

### results.json Format

The JSON submission format is composed of a single JSON array containing entries for every query in all the images of the test set. Specifically, the JSON file should contain a list of objects, each with the following properties:
-	an *id* property, reporting the unique identifier of the query (e.g., 36331).
-	an *image_id* property, reporting the filename of the input egocentric image (e.g., ZY20210800002_H2_C5_N14_S121_s02_T3_00010.png). Multiple queries on the same image share the same image_id.
-	a *query* property, reporting the input VQA query, copied verbatim from the test set (e.g., "Please analyze the interaction in the image and segment the active objects.").
-	an *answer_vqa* property, reporting the predicted answer to the VQA query (answering sub-task). This should identify which objects need to be segmented, using <MSK>, <MSK_0>, <MSK_1>, ... placeholders (e.g., "The mask of the active toy car is <MSK>."). For no-target queries, the answer should indicate that no suitable results were found.
-	an *answer_caption* property, reporting the predicted interaction description (analyzing sub-task). This is a fluent, natural-language summary of the interaction depicted in the image (e.g., "A toy car is held by the right hand of the person in this image.").
-	a *mask* property, reporting the path to the predicted mask file relative to the mask/directory (e.g., "mask/36331.png"). For multi-target queries with N masks, provide a comma-separated list of paths or a single combined mask file. For no-target queries (with_mask: 0), set to null.
-	a *with_mask* property, reporting the mask existence indicator as an integer ('0' or '1'). '1' if the query refers to at least one object present in the image; '0' otherwise.


Example results.json:
```
{[
  "id": 36331,
  "image_id": "ZY20210800002_H2_C5_N14_S121_s02_T3_00010.png",
  "query": "Please analyze the interaction in the image and segment the active objects.",
  "answer_vqa": "The mask of the active toy car is <MSK>.",
  "answer_caption": "A toy car is held by the right hand of the person in this image.",
  "mask": "mask/36331.png",
  "with_mask": 1]
}
```

### Important Notes

For multi-target queries with N masks, provide a single combined mask file.
For no-target queries (with_mask: 0), set mask to null.
The query field must be copied verbatim from the test set — do not paraphrase.
Mask files must be PNG images placed under the mask/ directory, named by query ID.
	
## Step 5: Upload Your Submission

Return to the My Submissions tab on the competition page.
Click the paper clip icon and select your ZIP file.
Your submission will be processed automatically. Once complete, you can view your score on the Results tab (Leaderboard).
	
## Step 6: Check the Leaderboard

Your score will appear on the leaderboard after evaluation. You may submit multiple times per day during the development phase. The final ranking is determined by your best submission.
pages.content_zh:
# 如何参与

## 步骤1：创建Codabench账户

访问 Codabench.org 并点击右上角的"注册"。您需要提供姓名和有效的电子邮件地址。注册完成后，您可以浏览并加入任何公开的基准测试。

## 步骤2：注册Ego-IRGBench

前往 Ego-IRG Challenge 竞赛页面，点击"我的提交"标签。系统将提示您接受竞赛的条款和条件。由于这是一个启用了自动批准的公开挑战赛，您在接受规则后即可立即参与。

## 步骤3：下载数据集并准备模型

Ego-IRGBench 数据集托管在 [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/yuki3585/Ego-IEGBench) 上。请根据官方 [ANNEXE 仓库](https://yuggiehk.github.io/annexe/) 中的说明下载并准备数据。该数据集包含超过 2 万张第一人称视角图像，带有 160 万个查询-答案-掩码对，分为训练集、验证集和测试集。

在训练集上训练您的模型，并在测试集上生成预测结果。

## 步骤4：准备提交的ZIP文件

您的提交必须是单个 ZIP 文件（.zip），结构如下：

```text
submission/
├── results.json            # 主要结果文件（必需）
├── mask/                   # 预测的像素级定位掩码（必需）
│   ├── <query_id>.png
│   └── ...
├── depth/                  # 预测的深度图（可选）
│   └── <image_id>.png
└── README.md               # 方法摘要（可选）
```

### results.json 格式

JSON 提交格式由单个 JSON 数组组成，包含测试集中所有图像的每个查询条目。具体而言，JSON 文件应包含一个对象列表，每个对象具有以下属性：
- *id* 属性，报告查询的唯一标识符（例如，36331）。
- *image_id* 属性，报告输入的第一人称视角图像的文件名（例如，ZY20210800002_H2_C5_N14_S121_s02_T3_00010.png）。同一图像上的多个查询共享相同的 image_id。
- *query* 属性，报告输入的视觉问答（VQA）查询，从测试集中逐字复制（例如，"Please analyze the interaction in the image and segment the active objects."）。
- *answer_vqa* 属性，报告对 VQA 查询的预测答案（回答子任务）。这应该识别需要分割哪些对象，使用 <MSK>、<MSK_0>、<MSK_1>、... 等占位符（例如，"The mask of the active toy car is <MSK>."）。对于无目标查询，答案应表明未找到合适的结果。
- *answer_caption* 属性，报告预测的交互描述（分析子任务）。这是对图像中所描绘交互的流畅自然语言总结（例如，"A toy car is held by the right hand of the person in this image."）。
- *mask* 属性，报告相对于 mask/ 目录的预测掩码文件路径（例如，"mask/36331.png"）。对于具有 N 个掩码的多目标查询，提供逗号分隔的路径列表或单个合并的掩码文件。对于无目标查询（with_mask: 0），设置为 null。
- *with_mask* 属性，报告掩码存在指示符，为整数（'0' 或 '1'）。如果查询涉及图像中至少一个对象，则为 '1'；否则为 '0'。

results.json 示例：
```
{[
  "id": 36331,
  "image_id": "ZY20210800002_H2_C5_N14_S121_s02_T3_00010.png",
  "query": "Please analyze the interaction in the image and segment the active objects.",
  "answer_vqa": "The mask of the active toy car is <MSK>.",
  "answer_caption": "A toy car is held by the right hand of the person in this image.",
  "mask": "mask/36331.png",
  "with_mask": 1]
}
```

### 重要说明

对于具有 N 个掩码的多目标查询，请提供单个合并的掩码文件。
对于无目标查询（with_mask: 0），将 mask 设置为 null。
query 字段必须从测试集中逐字复制——不要改写。
掩码文件必须是放置在 mask/ 目录下的 PNG 图像

pages.content:
##
Pan-cancer Segmentation in CT Images (Task2): RECIST to 3D
--- Organ and cancer segmentation in medical images, especially from 3D CT scans, is fundamentally important for accurate diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring the progression of diseases. This competition aims to facilitate the development of pan-cancer segmentation models in general CT scans with three main features: - [RECIST](https://doi.org/10.3389/fonc.2021.800547) (2D diameter marker) to 3D segmentation on laptop (without using GPU during inference) - Dataset: 10,000+ CT scans, covering whole-body cancer types - Evaluation Metrics: segmentation accuracy (DSC, NSD) and segmentation efficiency (running time and GPU consumption with tolerance) --- ## 🚀 Join the challenge (2026.04.01-8.30) #### Step 1. Join the challenge and download the data * Register an account on this website and join the challenge * Fill out the [registration form](https://forms.gle/my1MimQ758oDyhWb9). Note: To change team information, please simply re-submit the form. * Request Dataset [Subtask 2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/FLARE-MedFM/FLARE-Task1-PancancerRECIST-to-3D) * Submit the [Task2-baseline](https://drive.google.com/file/d/16nz_2UJLvsaVoqF1_oIWffu7J6UaU5UA/view?usp=drive_link) on [My Submission](https://www.codabench.org/competitions/7149/#/participate-tab) to test your account. Note: * Participants can join just one subtask or both tasks. * Public pre-trained models are allowed to use but please first post the model link in [forum](https://www.codabench.org/forums/7048/1161/) by April 1, 2026. --- ## 🏊‍ Validation submission (2026.4.20-8.30) * All teams can directly submit the segmentation results on the challenge page to get the segmentation accuracy metrics. * All teams can also make docker submissions. To avoid submission jams, each team can make one docker submission per month. * To make docker submissions, please send us (medseg20s@gmail.com): (Email subject: PanCancerSeg-YourTeamName-TeamLeaderName-Validation Submission) (1) a download link to your Docker container (teamname.tar.gz). (2) a sanity test video record. Please test your docker on validation cases and record the prediction process. For each case, the running time should be within 60s. * When the evaluation is finished, we will return back the metrics via email. ### Baseline Repo:https://github.com/medfm-flare/MedSAM2-RECIST ### Baseline result download [here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/16nz_2UJLvsaVoqF1_oIWffu7J6UaU5UA/view?usp=drive_link) (Same in step1) ### Submission format Submit a single ZIP whose contents sit in one flat directory (no sub-folders): ``` submission.zip ├── Colon_001.npz # one .npz per case ├── Kidney_001.npz ├── Liver_001.npz └── ... ``` **Segmentation masks** — one file per case, named `{identifier}.npz` (e.g. `Colon_001.npz`), stored under the array key `segs`, dtype `uint8`, with the same shape as the input `imgs` array `(D, H, W)`. ```python np.savez_compressed("Colon_001.npz", segs=segs.astype(np.uint8)) ``` **Instance labels must be preserved** — lesion `k` is labeled with id `k`, matching the id of its RECIST prompt in the input `recist` array: | Input `recist` label | Your `segs` label | Scored against | |---|---|---| | `1` | `1` | GT lesion `1` | | `2` | `2` | GT lesion `2` | | `3` | `3` | GT lesion `3` | Metrics are computed **per lesion**, so a mask that merges all lesions into label `1` scores near zero on multi-lesion cases. **Metrics:** | Metric | Description | |---|---| | `Lesion_DSC` | Dice, computed per lesion id | | `Lesion_NSD` | Normalized Surface Distance per lesion id, tolerance = 1.0 mm | Notes: * Do **not** wrap the files in a top-level folder — the scorer looks for `{identifier}.npz` directly, so a nested directory means every case is reported missing and the score is 0. * Filenames must match the test-set identifiers exactly (case-sensitive) so predictions can be paired with the ground truth; missing cases are scored 0. * A `segs` shape that differs from the reference volume scores the whole case 0. * Every lesion id present in the reference counts toward the case mean, so missed lesions are penalized rather than skipped. Extra ids not present in the reference are ignored. * Efficiency (runtime / memory) is not measured by the scoring program. --- ## 🏹 Testing submission (2026.9.1-9.7) * To avoid overfitting the testing set, **we only offer one successful submission opportunity on the testing set**. * The submission should include: (Email subject: PanCancerSeg-YourTeamName-TeamLeaderName-Testing Submission) (1) a download link to your Docker container (teamname.tar.gz); (2) a sanity test video record (download [example](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1uwbvYaSDQSxUT-yzGvuVcn6Ed3zNV1B3/view)). Please test your docker on validation cases and record the prediction process. For each case, the running time should be within 60s. * The submitted Docker container will be evaluated with the following commands. If the Docker container does not work or the paper does not include all the necessary information to reproduce the method, we will return back the error information and review comments to participants. - Task 1 docker load -i teamname.tar.gz docker container run --gpus "device=1" -m 28G --name teamname --rm -v \$PWD/PanCancerSeg_Test/:/workspace/inputs/ -v \$PWD/teamname_outputs/:/workspace/outputs/ teamname:latest /bin/bash -c "sh predict.sh" - Task 2 (CPU Only) docker load -i teamname.tar.gz docker container run -m 8G --name teamname --rm -v \$PWD/PanCancerSeg_Test/:/workspace/inputs/ -v \$PWD/teamname_outputs/:/workspace/outputs/ teamname:latest /bin/bash -c "sh predict.sh" ## Paper Submission (Due on Sept.14) Please follow the [template](https://www.overleaf.com/read/qcjybbkxtfyp#e3ce3b) to prepare the manuscript and submit it on [openreview](https://openreview.net/group?id=MICCAI.org/2026/Challenge/FLARE). --- ## 🏆 Awards - If there are more than 20 testing docker submissions, we will provide cash prizes for the top 3 teams (Amazon gift cards with 300/200/100 CAD, respectively) and souvenirs for the top 4-10 teams. Otherwise, only certificates will be provided. - The winning teams will be invited to give oral presentations. - The first author of the top 3 teams will be invited to contribute to a challenge summary paper. - A certificate will be awarded to the top 10 teams. (Top teams should make their code publicly available on GitHub for reproducibility.) - All teams have the opportunity to publish their methods in the challenge proceeding (Tentative LNCS, EI Index). [Here](https://link.springer.com/conference/flare) is an example of our previous Challenge. The challenge summary paper will be submitted to top-tired journals. Here are some of our previous summaries: * "[Fast and low-GPU-memory abdomen CT organ segmentation: the flare challenge.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.media.2022.102616)" Medical Image Analysis 82: 102616 (2022) * "[Unleashing the strengths of unlabelled data in deep learning-assisted pan-cancer abdominal organ quantification: the FLARE22 challenge](https://doi.org/10.1016/S2589-7500(24)00154-7)" The Lancet Digital Health, 6 (11), e815 - e826 (2024) * "[The multimodality cell segmentation challenge: toward universal solutions.](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-024-02233-6)" Nature Methods 21, 1103–1113 (2024).

# Dataset
The data download link will be sent to approved teams via email. Please make sure that you can download large files from Google Drive or Baidu Netdisk and have enough space and computing resources to process them.

Training set: 10000+ CT scans

Validation set: 100 CT scans with various cancer types

Testing set: 500 CT scans with various cancer types

Folder structure (download link will be sent to registered qualified participants):

Train-Labeled: This is a partially labeled dataset. Only the primary lesion is labeled in each case. The other lesions may not be labeled (e.g., metastatic lesions). In the final testing set, all the lesions are labeled. Participants can only use the image data for model development. Additional clinical data will not be provided.

Train-Unlabel (optional to use): only images are provided and the lesion annotations are not available. For the abdominal images, we also provide the pseudo labels, which are generated by the FLARE23 winning solution.

Validation-Public: Both images and annotations are provided. Please do not use them for model training!

Validation-Hidden: The labels of hidden validation set will not be released. Please submit the segmentation results on codabench to get the metrics.

Note:

Please do not use the public validaiton set for model training!
The testing set will also contain healthy cases (no lesion). Please pay attention to the false positives.
All the hidden testing images are from new centers, which will not be released during the challenge. Please submit the docker container of your algorithm and organizers will evaluate it on the hidden testing set.
Public Datasets and Models
Public datasets and models are allowed to use in this challenge (e.g., CT-RATE, Merlin) . To make sure all participants can access the same public datasets and models, please post the dataset and model links in forum by July 31.

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
# Evaluation
Segmentation accuracy metrics:

Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)
Normalized Surface Distance (NSD)
Segmentation efficiency metrics:

Running time (s). We give running time a tolerance of 45s (including the docker starting time). Moreover, the inference time for each case should be within 60s. Otherwise, the corresponding case will be regarded as a failed case (DSC=0, NSD=0).
running time

GPU memory consumption (area under GPU memory-time curve).
gpu memory

All metrics will be used to compute the ranking. We give GPU memory consumption a 4GB tolerance, GPU Memory = max(0, Real GPU Memory-4096MB) because all the previous top teams (i.e., FLARE21-23) can achieve state-of-the-art segmentation accuracy within this tolerance. We also give running time a tolerance (the running time of the winning solution in FLARE 2023) because it satisfies the typical clinical requirements and the code has been publicly available.

Evaluation code has been publicly available at: https://github.com/JunMa11/FLARE

```
docker load -i teamname.tar.gz
docker container run -m 8G --name teamname --rm -v $PWD/PanCancerSeg_Test/:/workspace/inputs/ -v $PWD/teamname_outputs/:/workspace/outputs/ teamname:latest /bin/bash -c "sh predict.sh"
```
## Evaluation Platform
The submitted docker containers will be evaluated on a Ubuntu 20.04 desktop. Detailed information is listed as follows:

CPU: Intel® Xeon(R) W-2133 CPU @ 3.60GHz × 12
GPU: NVIDIA QUADRO RTX5000 (16G)
RAM: 28G
Driver Version: 510.39.01
CUDA Version: 11.6
Docker version 20.10.13
## Ranking Scheme
Following the recommendation in ChallengeR [1], the ranking scheme includes the following three steps:

Step 1. For each testing case, we compute the four metrics;

Step 2. Rank participants for each of the 500 testing cases and each metric; Thus, each participant will have 2000 (500x4) rankings.

Step 3. Average all these rankings.

NTIRE 2026: 3D Content Super-Resolution Challenge

Important Dates

  • 2026-01-15: Release of training and validation data;
  • 2026-01-30: Validation server online;
  • 2026-03-10: Final test data release, validation server closed;
  • 2026-03-17: Test result submission deadline;

  • 2026-03-22: Challenge paper submission deadline;

  • 2026-04-08: Camera-ready;
  • 2026-06-18 (TBU): Workshop day;

Introduction

Beyond traditional images and videos, 3D content has gained immense popularity to provide both appearance and geometry information of the scene. Recent years have witnessed exponential surge of 3D contents due to the advances in 3D generation and reconstruction. Nevertheless, current 3D generation models still suffer relatively low quality. For 3D reconstruction, due to diverse constraints in the real world, the observed multi-view images are usually of low resolution, which ultimately degrades the quality of reconstructed 3D content. In applications like AR/VR, increasing the resolution of these 3D contents is highly demanded to provide immersive experience and help to parse the real world.
Recently, remarkable progress has been achieved in image super-resolution (SR) to improve the visual quality of images. To enhance the quality of a 3D content, a straightforward approach is to employ an off-the-shelf image SR model to super-resolve the rendered images. However, this approach ignores the tightly coupled relationship between geometry and appearance information, resulting in multi-view inconsistency and flicker artifacts.
In this challenge, we aim at establishing a benchmark for 3D content SR. We aspire to highlight the specific challenges and research problems faced by 3D content SR. We hope that this challenge could inspire the community to explore the cross area of low-level vision and 3D vision, and ultimately drive technological advancement in emerging applications such as AR/VR.

Challenge Description

The 8th edition of NTIRE: New Trends in Image Restoration and Enhancement workshop will be held on June, 2026 in conjunction with CVPR 2026.
The objective of this challenge is to reconstruct high-resolution (HR) 3D contents from their low-resolution (LR) counterparts. During the development phase, the validation set will be released. The participants can evaluate their models on the validation set by submitting their results to the validation server. Specifically, super-resolved images are rendered under given camera intrinsics and extrinsics and then submitted to the server for online evaluation. During the test phase, the test set will be released, which includes LR 3D content only. Challenge participants should apply their trained models to the LR 3D content to generate super-resolved results. Then, these results are submitted to the server and evaluated by the organizers.
This challenge has two tracks:
  • Track 1: Bicubic Degradation
    • The aim of this track is to obtain super-resolved 3D content under bicubic degradation (Matlab $imresize$ function in bicubic mode).
  • Track 2: Realistic Degradation
    • The aim of this track is to obtain super-resolved 3D content under realistic degradation.

简介

除了传统的图像和视频外，3D内容因其能够提供场景的外观和几何信息而获得了极大的普及。近年来，由于3D生成和重建技术的进步，3D内容呈现指数级增长。然而，当前的3D生成模型仍然存在质量相对较低的问题。对于3D重建而言，由于现实世界中各种约束条件，观测到的多视图图像通常分辨率较低，这最终降低了重建3D内容的质量。在AR/VR等应用中，提高这些3D内容的分辨率对于提供沉浸式体验和帮助解析现实世界具有强烈需求。
近年来，图像超分辨率(SR)在提高图像视觉质量方面取得了显著进展。为了增强3D内容的质量，一种直接的方法是使用现成的图像超分辨率模型对渲染图像进行超分辨率处理。然而，这种方法忽略了几何信息和外观信息之间的紧密耦合关系，导致多视图不一致和闪烁伪影。
在本挑战赛中，我们旨在为3D内容超分辨率建立一个基准。我们希望突出3D内容超分辨率所面临的特定挑战和研究问题。我们希望本次挑战赛能够激励社区探索底层视觉和3D视觉的交叉领域，并最终推动AR/VR等新兴应用的技术进步。

挑战赛描述

第八届NTIRE：图像恢复与增强新趋势研讨会将于2026年6月与CVPR 2026联合举办。
本次挑战赛的目标是从低分辨率(LR)3D内容重建高分辨率(HR)3D内容。在开发阶段，将发布验证集。参与者可以通过将结果提交到验证服务器来评估他们在验证集上的模型。具体而言，在给定相机内参和外参的条件下渲染超分辨率图像，然后提交到服务器进行在线评估。 在测试阶段，将发布测试集，其中仅包含低分辨率3D内容。挑战赛参与者应将训练好的模型应用于低分辨率3D内容以生成超分辨率结果。然后，将这些结果提交到服务器并由组织者进行评估。
本次挑战赛设有两个赛道：
  • 赛道1：双三次退化
    • 本赛道旨在获得在双三次退化（Matlab的$imresize$函数双三次模式）下的超分辨率3D内容。
  • 赛道2：真实退化
    • 本赛道旨在获得在真实退化下的超分辨率3D内容。

NTIRE 2026: 3D Content Super-Resolution Challenge

Evaluation

The objective of this challenge is to reconstruct high-resolution (HR) 3D contents from their low-resolution (LR) counterparts. During the development and testing phase, challenge participants will submit the super-resolved results. Example codes to calculate evaluation metrics can be found here.
  • Track 1: Bicubic Degradation
    • Given multi-view images of a scene, bicubic degradation (Matlab $imresize$ function in bicubic mode) is used to generate LR images.
  • Track 2: Realistic Degradation
    • Given multi-view images of a scene, a realistic degradation model consisting of random blur, downsampling, noise, and compression is adopted to synthesize LR images.
For quantitative evaluation, we select M camera poses for each test 3D content to render M images and corresponding depth maps. Then, PSNR is used to evaluate the visual quality, while EPE is employed to assess geometry accuracy. The final score for ranking is calculated as:

Submission

During the development phase, participants can submit their results on the validation set to get feedback from the Codabench server. During the test phase, participants will submit the whole results of the test set. This should match the last submission to Codabench.
The submitted results should contain images and depth maps (1368x912) rendered from the super-resolved 3D content under given camera intrinsics and extrinsics. Note that, the intrinsics and extrinsics file can be found here (validation poses and test poses), and the camera indices in the following example code should be used for rendering.

When submitting the results, create a ZIP archive containing all the resulting images and depth maps. The terminology of the rendered images and depth maps should be identical to that of the camera intrinsics and extrinsics in the validation and test sets. A valid example dummy submission file can be found here.
After the test phase, the participants will 1) fill in an online form and 2) submit a zip file (containing fact sheet, source code, and final results, an example of fact sheet can be found here) to the official submission account (ntire.3dsr@outlook.com) by email. The final submission should be made by the following rules:
  • The submitted results must be from the same method that generated the last submission to the Codabench. We will check the consistency. Otherwise, the submission is invalid.
  • Both the testing source code (or executable) and the training code must be submitted. Reproducibility is a necessary condition.
  • Factsheet describing the method details should be submitted together. The factsheet format is provided with data. Participants must submit a compiled pdf file and the tex source. We encourage participants to provide details and enclose figure image sources together. This helps writing the challenge summary report.
Each participating team in the final testing phase should use the provided factsheet template to describe their solution(s).

Email submission format

Please use the following format to submit your final results, fact sheet, code, and model (with trained parameters). We will run the test code to reproduce the results. The code and the model will be posted on the NTIRE 2026 website.

to: ntire.3dsr@outlook.com;
cc: your_team_members
title: [NTIRE 2026 3D Content Super-Resolution Challenge (Track *)] - [Team_name]
body should include:
1) the challenge name (including track id)
2) team name
3) team leader's name, affiliation, and email address
4) team members' names, affiliations, and email addresses
5) user name on the NTIRE 2026 Codabench leaderboard (if any)
6) executable/source code attached or download links.
7) fact sheet attached
8) download link to the results

Introduction

Beyond traditional images and videos, 3D content has gained immense popularity to provide both appearance and geometry information of the scene. Recent years have witnessed exponential surge of 3D contents due to the advances in 3D generation and reconstruction. Nevertheless, current 3D generation models still suffer relatively low quality. For 3D reconstruction, due to diverse constraints in the real world, the observed multi-view images are usually of low resolution, which ultimately degrades the quality of reconstructed 3D content. In applications like AR/VR, increasing the resolution of these 3D contents is highly demanded to provide immersive experience and help to parse the real world.
Recently, remarkable progress has been achieved in image super-resolution (SR) to improve the visual quality of images. To enhance the quality of a 3D content, a straightforward approach is to employ an off-the-shelf image SR model to super-resolve the rendered images. However, this approach ignores the tightly coupled relationship between geometry and appearance information, resulting in multi-view inconsistency and flicker artifacts.
In this challenge, we aim at establishing a benchmark for 3D content SR. We aspire to highlight the specific challenges and research problems faced by 3D content SR. We hope that this challenge could inspire the community to explore the cross area of low-level vision and 3D vision, and ultimately drive technological advancement in emerging applications such as AR/VR.

Challenge Description

The 8th edition of NTIRE: New Trends in Image Restoration and Enhancement workshop will be held on June, 2026 in conjunction with CVPR 2026.
The objective of this challenge is to reconstruct high-resolution (HR) 3D contents from their low-resolution (LR) counterparts. During the development phase, the validation set will be released. The participants can evaluate their models on the validation set by submitting their results to the validation server. Specifically, super-resolved images are rendered under given camera intrinsics and extrinsics and then submitted to the server for online evaluation. During the test phase, the test set will be released, which includes LR 3D content only. Challenge participants should apply their trained models to the LR 3D content to generate super-resolved results. Then, these results are submitted to the server and evaluated by the organizers.
This challenge has two tracks:
  • Track 1: Bicubic Degradation
    • The aim of this track is to obtain super-resolved 3D content under bicubic degradation (Matlab $imresize$ function in bicubic mode).
  • Track 2: Realistic Degradation
    • The aim of this track is to obtain super-resolved 3D content under realistic degradation.

If you fail to follow these terms, you will be removed from the competition. In your submission, you MUST provide name, affiliation (with contact information) and a short description of the method with a link to a GitHub repository. ## Download the dataset The dataset, **FOR-wood**, is available for download from Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23012506 ## Benchmarking For evaluation the participant should use their model on the downloaded test set to predict either whorl-positions relative to the ground, the stem profile diameter, or both and output two tables (*.csv) containing predictions for all trees in the test data set. For the whorl detection task, submit a `branch_references.csv` table with the following columns and capitalization: `TreeID`, `Z`, `whorl_number` The scorer matches predictions using `TreeID` and `Z`, where `Z` is the whorl height in metres and `whorl_number` identifies the whorl order. |TreeID|Z|whorl_number| |---|---|---| |221|10.8434|1| |221|11.2577|2| |221|11.5477|3| |n|...|...| For the stem profile prediction task, submit a `stem_references.csv` table with the following columns and capitalization: `TreeID`, `Z`, `D` `Z` is the height in metres and `D` is the predicted stem diameter in metres. Provide values at 0.6 m, 1.3 m, 2 m, and then every metre up the length of the tree. If values are not provided exactly at the evaluation heights, the scorer linearly interpolates the submitted profile. |TreeID|Z|D| |---|---|---| |313|0.4903|0.30539| |313|1.1375|0.29004| |313|1.8426|0.27856| |313|4.8407|0.25084| |n|...|...| Make sure that the column names are exactly the same as stated here. The zip archive itself can be named anything, but it may contain either or both CSV files, and each included file must use its exact corresponding filename: ```text your_submission.zip ├── branch_references.csv └── stem_references.csv ``` ## Submission limits You may submit up to 2 times per day (20 total for the phase). The daily limit is set to 2 rather than 1 so that if a submission errors out (e.g. a naming or column mismatch), you still have a same-day chance to fix it and resubmit. ## Viewing your results After submitting, publish your result to the leaderboard from your submissions panel. The leaderboard is sorted by F1 (whorl detection) by default - if you only submitted stem profile predictions, click on a stem profile column header (e.g. RMSE (Stem)) to sort the leaderboard by that metric instead and see where your submission ranks.

## SingleTree项目 SingleTree项目旨在通过关注单株树木来创建更智能的林业系统。这种方法将帮助森林适应气候变化、变得更具韧性，并实现木材资源的更可持续利用。SingleTree将开发基于人工智能和遥感的先进森林监测方法、自适应单株级管理解决方案、用于实施单株作业的智能机械，以及在价值链早期提高可追溯性和预测木材质量的能力，作为优化生物质供应的基础。 欲了解更多信息，请访问 https://singletree.eu/
# 基准测试目标 本基准测试的目标是收集和评估传感器与平台无关的节疤检测和干形算法的性能。结果将为SingleTree项目提供可在项目链下游使用的方法。 # 奖项 排名前五的参与者将有机会共同撰写一篇关于本基准测试的论文。每个团队可提名最多两人作为共同作者注册。 # 如何参与 ## 阅读参赛条款 进入"开始使用"下的条款选项卡，阅读参赛条款。如果您未能遵守这些条款，将被取消参赛资格。 在您的提交材料中，**必须**提供姓名、所属机构（含联系信息）以及方法的简短描述，并附上GitHub仓库链接。 ## 下载数据集 数据集 **FOR-wood** 可从Zenodo下载：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23012506 ## 基准测试 为进行评估，参与者应使用其模型对下载的测试集进行预测，预测相对于地面的节疤位置、干形直径，或两者兼而有之，并输出两个包含测试数据集中所有树木预测的表格（*.csv）。 对于节疤检测任务，提交包含以下列及大小写的 `branch_references.csv` 表格： `TreeID`、`Z`、`whorl_number` 评分器使用 `TreeID` 和 `Z` 进行预测匹配，其中 `Z` 为节疤高度（米），`whorl_number` 标识节疤序号。 |TreeID|Z|whorl_number| |---|---|---| |221|10.8434|1| |221|11.2577|2| |221|11.5477|3| |n|...|...| 对于干形预测任务，提交包含以下列及大小写的 `stem_references.csv` 表格： `TreeID`、`Z`、`D` `Z` 为高度（米），`D` 为预测的树干直径（米）。 请在 0.6 米、1.3 米、2 米处提供数值，然后沿树高每米提供一个数值。如果未在评估高度处精确提供数值，评分器将对提交的轮廓进行线性插值。 |TreeID|Z|D| |---|---|---| |313|0.4903|0.30539| |313|1.1375|0.29004| |313|1.8426|0.27856| |313|4.8407|0.25084| |n|...|...| 确保列名与此处所述完全一致。zip压缩包本身可以任意命名，但可以包含一个或两个CSV文件，且每个包含的文件必须使用其确切对应的文件名： ```text your_submission.zip ├── branch_references.csv └── stem_references.csv ``` ## 提交限制 您每天最多可提交 2 次（本阶段共 20 次）。每日限制设为 2 次而非 1 次，是为了防止提交出错（如命名或列不匹配）时，您仍有机会在当天修复并重新提交。 ## 查看结果 提交后，从您的提交面板将结果发布到排行榜。排行榜默认按 F1（节疤检测）排序——如果您仅提交了干形预测，请点击干形列标题（如 RMSE（树干））以按该指标排序排行榜并查看您的排名。

# Dataset
For this benchmark, we have assembled a dataset consisting of indivdual tree point clouds together with annotations describing whorl positions along the stem as well as stem taper. The data has been pooled from Sweden, Finland and Norway and consists mainly of Scott's Pine trees with a smaller proportion Norway Spruce. 

The dataset, **FOR-wood**, is available for download from Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23012506

The data consist of:
* **Training data**: tree point clouds (laz files) with whorl and taper annotations (`branch_references.csv`, `stem_references.csv`)
* **Test data**: only tree point clouds (laz files), no annotations
